Sky Princess Review

Review of Sky Princess

The 2019-built Sky Princess cruise ship is the fourth Royal-class vessel in the Princess Cruises fleet, together with the fleetmates Royal Princess (2013), Regal Princess (2014), Majestic Princess (2017), Enchanted Princess (2021), and Discovery Princess (2022). From the same class is also the P&O UK liner Britannia (2015).

The vessel (IMO number 9802396) is currently Bermuda-flagged (MMSI 310780000) and registered in Hamilton.

History - construction and ownership

Princess Cruises is a USA-based passenger shipping company headquartered in Beverly Hills, CA. Formerly a subsidiary of P&O Princess Cruises (founded in 1977), the company merged with Carnival Corporation in 2003—the world’s largest cruise shipowner. Among Princess Cruise Lines Ltd’s assets is the Caribbean private island resort Princess Cays (located on the southern end of Eleuthera Island in the Bahamas), approximately 80 km (50 mi) from Nassau.

The 3600-passenger ship Sky Princess is among the largest cruise ships sailing the seas. The vessel was built at the Fincantieri shipyard in Italy and has 19 decks. Sky Princess features 16 bars and restaurants, a luxury spa, and unique attractions such as the glass-enclosed SeaWalk walkway extending over the ocean.

Decks and Cabins

Sky Princess staterooms (1834 total in 38 categories) include 1438 cabins (80% of all) with step-out balconies. The ship also has 36 wheelchair-accessible cabins and no Oceanview-category cabins. The largest accommodations are the 2-Room Sky Suites (950-1010 ft2 / 88-94 m2 plus 700 ft2 / 65 m2 terrace).

The vessel has 18 decks, of which 15 are passenger-accessible and 10 contain cabins.

Sky Suites (a new cabin category) are Princess Cruises’ first staterooms designed for up to 5 guests and offering 270-degree top-deck views. These are also the fleet’s largest cabins and feature the fleet’s largest balconies. Both Sky Suites are located midship on Sports Deck 18 (portside and starboard). Each suite has a wraparound terrace and provides a private view of the outdoor “Movies Under the Stars” theater (the fleet’s largest outdoor LED screen).

Shipboard dining options - Food and Drinks

There are many for-fee dining options onboard Sky Princess, but guests who prefer not to pay extra are still offered a wide variety of quality complimentary choices. Those who prefer traditional dining can choose between the three main dining rooms: Allegro, Concerto, and Symphony.

Horizon Court and Horizon Bistro provide buffet-style dining in a casual setting. Passengers who want a quick bite by the pool can grab a burger from Trident Grill or a slice from Prego Pizzeria. Indoors, Alfredo’s serves calzones, salads, and thin-crust pizza. Allegro Dining Room is the only option offering traditional fixed seating for complimentary dinner, with seatings at 5:45 p.m. or 8:15 p.m. Allegro’s menus are diverse and typically include soup or salad, appetizers, pasta, and main entrées, along with a special dessert menu.

Follows the complete list of Sky Princess restaurants and food bars.

  • Symphony Restaurant (midship location; offers “Anytime Dining” for dinner; includes the “Wine Cellar” area serving the “Wine Maker’s Dinner” for $40, capacity 12 guests)
  • Alfredo’s Pizzeria (121 seats; the largest complimentary pizzeria at sea)
  • Concerto Restaurant (forward dining room; offers “Anytime Dining” from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m.; serves the “Wine Maker’s Dinner” package for $40)
  • Allegro Restaurant (aft dining room; offers formal dining with two fixed dinner seatings at 6 p.m. or 8:15 p.m.; includes the “Chef’s Table Lumiere” private dining experience for $115, limited to 12 guests)
  • OceanFront is a specialty seafood bar with an a-la-carte menu (sushi, sashimi).
  • Crown Grill (160-seat steakhouse/seafood restaurant, reservations recommended; on select days also serves complimentary British Pub Lunch)
  • Salty Dog Grill (Deck 5) and Alfredo's Pizzeria (Deck 7 / fleet’s largest) are self-serve complimentary fast-food venues. The rustic Salty Dog Gastropub is a venue where passengers can watch sporting events, enjoy small bites and drinks, and try the Ernesto Burger by chef-partner Ernesto Uchimura (founding chef of the original Umami Burger and owner of the LA-based restaurant and bar Electric Owl).
  • Calypso Cabana (food bar offering picnic baskets, desserts, champagne, and wine packages)
  • World Fresh Marketplace (self-service buffet restaurant, complimentary); Horizon Buffet (indoor seating) and Horizon Terrace (outdoor seating)
  • Swirls Bar (ice cream)

Sabatini’s Trattoria (a la carte-priced specialty restaurant on Deck 7) offers a three-course Italian/seafood menu. Sabatini’s is open between 6 p.m. and 11 p.m., and reservations are recommended. The venue blends contemporary spaciousness with classic Italian accents and features handmade pasta courses (created in partnership with celebrity chef Angelo Auriana) prepared daily. Sabatini’s Trattoria also offers “Sabatini’s Bites” during wine tastings.

Bistro Sur La Mer (cover charge US$35 per person) was an authentic Parisian bistro featuring a fine-dining dinner menu of French cuisine by Michelin-star chef Emmanuel Renaut. In 2023, La Mer was replaced with “The Catch by Rudi”—Princess Cruises’ first seafood-dedicated restaurant (introduced on Enchanted Princess) created in partnership with celebrity chef Rudi Sodamin, who also serves as Head of Princess Culinary Arts (onboard dining program).

  • The menu focuses primarily on seafood dishes based on the freshest catch (sustainably sourced seafood from the current itinerary’s ports of call) but also includes surf-and-turf options (including prime beef steaks), vegetarian dishes, gourmet appetizers, and desserts.
  • The specialty dining experience features creative food presentations, distinctive settings, and guests being welcomed at the table with a cocktail crafted by Rob Floyd (celebrity mixologist and liquid chef).
  • The menu includes “The Daily Catch” items (featuring sustainably sourced seafood from local ports of call), international fusion influences (such as Asian-fried calamari), Rudi Sodamin’s contemporary interpretations of classic dishes (such as lobster with garlic butter crust), and signature creations from his personal repertoire (including Towering Trio and Whole Dover Sole). The Seafood Trolley presentation includes lobster tails, shrimp, oysters, mussels, and other seafood.
  • The Catch by Rudi’s wine selection is carefully curated to pair with seafood. The waitstaff, trained by sommeliers, offer recommendations for white, red, rosé, and sparkling wines from coastal wine-growing regions.

The Catch by Rudi’s cover charge is US$39 per person and is also included in the Princess Premier package (premium add-on).

In 2024, three distinct dining styles were introduced fleetwide: Traditional (early/late seating), Reservable, and Walk-in Anytime (open seating). Each ship designates three separate dining rooms to accommodate these options, which are integrated with the OceanNow service, allowing guests to order anything at any time and have it delivered anywhere on board.

Shipboard entertainment options - Fun and Sport

The majority of stage performances take place in the two-level Princess Theater (decks 6 and 7). This is the ship’s main show lounge with palladium-style seating and grand-style evening productions.

The theater lounge does not offer tables or drink holders, so guests who order a drink before the show will need to hold it. The entertainment program is excellent and varied, featuring innovative productions. In addition to production shows, the Princess Theater also hosts guest vocalists, instrumentalists, and other live performances.

Compared to other Royal-class ships, Sky Princess features the new aft-located Wakeview swimming pool, two deep-water top-deck pools, and the adults-only Retreat Pool, as well as additional Jacuzzis (including two cantilevered above the deep-water pools). The expanded Sanctuary area features a redesigned layout and twice as many private cabanas as sisterships. Vista Lounge has also been redesigned. Princess Live is a café serving quick bites, specialty teas, and barista-made coffees.

Follows the complete list of Sky Princess lounges, clubs, and entertainment venues for kids, teens, and adults.

  • The Piazza Atrium (three-deck open floor area featuring live performances and the lobby Bar Piazza)
  • Princess Fine Arts Gallery; Photo Gallery & Shop; Limelight Photo Studio; Platinum Studio
  • International Cafe (24-hour specialty coffee bar and patisserie)
  • Vines Bar (wine/seafood/sushi bar)
  • Gelato (the largest ice cream bar at sea)
  • Library (with Internet stations); Internet Cafe (24-hour)
  • Princess Theater (two-level venue hosting musical productions, workshops, seminars, and game shows)
  • Celebrations Shop; Calypso Cove Shop; Essence Shop; Meridian Bay Shop; Facets Shop
  • Club 6 Disco & Bar; Churchill’s Lounge & Bar (cigar bar); Bellini’s Bar; Crooners Lounge & Bar; Princess Live Lounge; Vista Lounge; Concierge Lounge (Suite guests only); SkyLight Bar; Seaview Bar
  • Princess Casino (gambling lounge and bar)
  • Wheelhouse Bar (piano bar by day and English-style pub at night)
  • Lotus Spa complex; Beauty Salon; Fitness Center (with Aerobics Studio)
  • Wedding Chapel
  • Movies Under the Stars (LED screen outdoor cinema)
  • The Game Lounge (video games arcade); Teen Center; Youth Center; Remix Disco & Lounge (teen club)
  • The Sanctuary (adult-only open-air relaxation complex)
  • SeaWalk (glass-bottomed cantilevered walkway, 18 m / 60 ft long)
  • Fountain Pool area; Retreat Pool area
  • Princess Sports Central - Center Court (volleyball, basketball, European football); table tennis, virtual gaming at the Game Lounge, The Greens golf nets, Golfing Cage, Laser Shooting, jogging track
  • "Take 5" (Deck 6 midship portside) is the world’s only jazz theater at sea. This jazz-themed lounge features a chic setting, live performances by renowned jazz musicians, handcrafted premium cocktails developed by Rob Floyd (master mixologist), guest performers, late-night themed parties, and daily enrichment programming with guest speakers and workshops. Custom media content is displayed on the lounge’s TV screens.

On the sisterships Enchanted and Sky, Princess Cruises introduced the exclusive “Jim Henson’s Inspired Silliness”—a 30-minute live production show inspired by Jim Henson’s puppetry works. James Maury Henson (1936-1990) was a US puppeteer, animator, cartoonist, actor, and filmmaker best known as the creator of “The Muppets” (TV show created in 1955). The cruise line’s production show (hosted in the Princess Theater) features singers and dancers, high-tech visuals, comedy acts, and professional puppetry. The show begins with a video introduction by Henson’s son Brian and includes new puppets from Henson’s Creature Shop along with newly designed characters.

The Experience Center (Deck 18 aft starboard) has a maximum capacity of six people and no age restrictions. This onboard Escape Room hosts the “Phantom Bridge” game, combining physical and virtual elements to create a unique puzzle-solving experience at sea. The attraction is part of Princess Cruises’ Discovery at SEA enrichment program and offers interactive adventure gaming experiences with more than 700 possible outcomes. Phantom Bridge sessions last approximately 23 minutes and allow passengers to navigate a virtual cruise liner, observe changing simulations, uncover clues, and solve puzzles. The technology includes a physical steering wheel and touch-screen surfaces, projection mapping, advanced sound and lighting effects, and hidden physical elements integrated throughout the ship.

Itineraries

Sky Princess’ itinerary program began with an inaugural Mediterranean cruise season in Europe. The program included 10 voyages with eight different itineraries. The inaugural cruise was scheduled for October 20, 2019.

The 7-night maiden voyage (October 20) was a one-way Adriatic and Mediterranean itinerary from Piraeus-Athens to Barcelona, visiting the ports of Kotor (Montenegro), Corfu (Greece), Messina (Sicily, Italy), and Naples (Italy). In November 2019, the ship operated a Transatlantic repositioning cruise (Nov 17–Dec 1) from Europe to Florida-Caribbean (14-day crossing from Barcelona to Fort Lauderdale).

The Caribbean cruise program is based on 7-day roundtrips from homeport Fort Lauderdale (starting December 1, 2019).

In summer 2020, the ship was scheduled to operate in Northern Europe, with homeports in Copenhagen (Denmark), Warnemunde-Rostock (Germany), and St Petersburg (Russia). Baltic Sea cruises were priced between USD 2300 and 2800 per person. In fall 2020, the liner was scheduled to be homeported in NYC New York for 7-day “Canada and New England” cruises (priced approximately USD 1000–1100 per person).

Sky Princess Wiki

The vessel's powerplant includes four Wartsila marine diesel engines (model 46F, 2x12V and 2x14V) with a combined power output of 62.4 MW (83,700 hp). The propulsion system is based on two azipods with a combined power output of 18 MW (24,000 hp).

The ship has Fincantieri Monfalcone yard/hull number 6268, volume 145281 GT-tons, DWT (deadweight tonnage) 11772 tons, LOA length 330 m, beam 38 m (maximum width 47 m, including the Navigation Bridge wings), and maximum draught 8.6 m.

In April 2016, Princess Cruises (via Carnival Corporation) signed a shipbuilding order for two new liners, scheduled for delivery in 2019 (Sky) and 2020 (Enchanted). These are the fourth and fifth Royal-class ships (same design as Royal, Regal, and Majestic) constructed at Fincantieri Monfalcone shipyard as part of a previous agreement between Carnival Corporation (shipowner) and Fincantieri (shipbuilder). At that time, Carnival Corp had a total of 16 shipbuilding orders scheduled for delivery between 2016 and 2020. All of these new liners are among the fleet's largest and feature Movies Under the Stars (outdoor theater), the Piazza Atrium, 80% balcony staterooms, and new dining venues.

In late January 2017, Carnival Corporation announced two additional shipbuilding orders. The new ships were ordered for the fleets of Princess (Royal-class / Discovery Princess) and Holland America Line (Pinnacle-class / Nieuw Rotterdam). Carnival signed an MoA (memorandum of agreement) with Fincantieri to construct both vessels, with scheduled deliveries in 2021 (for HAL, at the Marghera yard) and 2022 (for Princess, at the Monfalcone yard). By the time both contracts were finalized (February 2017), Carnival Corporation had a total of 19 new ships scheduled for delivery between 2017 and 2022.

The vessel's construction officially started with the steel-cutting ceremony on September 8, 2017. On July 5, 2018, the keel-laying ceremony was held at the Monfalcone shipyard, traditionally signifying the start of the vessel's physical construction. The building process mainly involves assembling prefabricated blocks (modular components) joined together at the yard's drydock facility.

Sky Princess was officially delivered to Princess Cruises on October 15, 2019, at the Monfalcone Shipyard. The ceremony was attended by Laura Castelli (Italy's Deputy Minister of Economy and Finance), Giuseppe Bono (Fincantieri's CEO), Micky Arison (Carnival Corporation's Chairman), Arnold Donald (Carnival Corporation's President and CEO), Stein Kruse (Group CEO for the subsidiaries Holland America, Seabourn, Carnival Australia, Carnival UK), and Jan Swartz (Group President of the subsidiaries Princess Cruises and Carnival Australia).

Sky Princess is the 17th vessel built by Fincantieri for Princess Cruises. As of October 2019, Fincantieri had built a total of 95 cruise liners (since 1990), of which 68 were for Carnival Corporation, with 49 more on order or under construction.

Fun facts: It takes approximately 3 million man-hours to build a Royal-class liner. About 37,000 tons of steel are used in its construction. For comparison, approximately 12,000 tons of steel were used to construct the Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles. The vessel requires about 95,000 gallons (360,000 L) of paint—roughly twice the quantity consumed for the Golden Gate Bridge (which is repainted annually). The electrical cables installed throughout the vessel are about 2484 mi (4000 km) long, enough to link NYC with LA.

The vessel was launched (floated out from drydock) on February 14, 2019. On the same day (February 14) the keel-laying ceremony was held for the sistership Enchanted Princess (2021), along with the steel-cutting ceremony for the sixth and final Royal-class liner Discovery Princess (2022). Sky Princess' float-out was led by godmother Kerry Ann Wright (Second Officer for Princess Cruises), nominated as Madrina by her fellow crew members. The ship's six-day Mediterranean Sea trials were successfully completed in early September.

Princess Cruises' Sky Princess was officially christened on December 7, 2019, in Port Everglades (Fort Lauderdale Florida USA). The liner has two godmothers (former NASA personnel) — Kathryn Patricia Hire (born 1959, former astronaut and now US Navy Reserve Captain) and Frances "Poppy" Northcutt (born 1943, NASA Apollo Program engineer).

The ship's first commanding officers were Heikki Laakkonen and Michele Tuvo (Captains), Fabio Braccelli and Mladen Ratkovic (Chief Engineers), Terri Cybuliak and Richard Harry (General Hotel Managers), and Giovanni Cardile and Brian Whelan (Staff Captains).

Sky Princess refurbishment 2023 review

The ship's first drydocking was in 2023 (April 19–May 6).

The 16-day project (conducted at Damen Verolme Rotterdam in Rotterdam Holland) was primarily for regularly scheduled maintenance works and minor technical upgrades.

It involved approximately 700 contractor workers in addition to the ship's own ~1200 crew members.

The work included installing a new air lubrication hull system, underwater hull cleaning and painting, and the renovation of some staterooms and public spaces. "The Catch by Rudi" (a new seafood restaurant) replaced "Bistro Sur La Mer".
